notes.source: the text of a Query Tool / View-Edit Data grid cell or column label, handed to web/pgadmin/static/js/utils.js:599 measureText(text, font) before the grid is laid out; the caller is outside the diff and a code search of the repository did not surface it
notes.sink: web/pgadmin/static/js/utils.js:605 measureText.ele.innerHTML = text - the measured text is parsed as HTML in a hidden div
notes.between: measureText only measures with getBoundingClientRect(); the same string is drawn into the grid afterwards. Nothing escapes or strips it on the way. The fix changes the assignment to textContent so the measurement div never parses the text. Second explanation: sink (a measuring helper is not an obvious sink).
notes.fix: uses textContent instead of innerHTML when measuring text

notes.source: webapp/content/js/dashboard.js:2887-2898 applyState() copies a loaded dashboard's saved timeConfig into TimeRange (relativeStartQuantity, relativeStartUnits, relativeUntilQuantity, relativeUntilUnits) - values another user saved through the dashboard save endpoint
notes.sink: dashboard.js:1184-1195 getTimeText() concatenates those values into a label, and dashboard.js:1198 updateTimeText() pushes it into the toolbar TextItem (tbtext at :556-560), which Ext renders as HTML
notes.between: dashboard load -> applyState(state) -> timeRangeUpdated()/updateTimeText() -> toolbar setText; there is no encoding anywhere. The fix runs the four fields through htmlStriped() (htmlEncode plus spaces to underscores) before storing them in TimeRange, tightens the quantity regex to /^\d+$/, and has the views reject dashboard names with restricted symbols. Second explanation: front-end.
notes.fix: HTML-encodes the time-range fields before they are saved or rendered, and restricts the dashboard-name route parameter

notes.source: airflow/www/static/js/ti_log.js:100-122 the log lines fetched for a task instance (the log endpoint returns the task's log text); every line goes through the URL linkifier
notes.sink: ti_log.js:120 .replace(urlRegex, (url) => `${url}`) followed by :122 logBlock.innerHTML += linkifiedMessage - a quote inside a URL in the log line leaves the href and adds attributes
notes.between: Logs/utils.ts:115-120 is the same path in the current log view (ansiUp.ansi_to_html then the urlRegex replace). Nothing escapes the URL before the template literal. The fix does not escape: it sets ansiUp.url_allowlist = {} in both renderers so AnsiUp stops producing links. Second explanation: sink (innerHTML built from a regex replacement).
notes.fix: turns off AnsiUp linkification (url_allowlist = {}) in both log renderers

notes.source: airflow/www/views.py:1685 origin = get_safe_url(request.values.get('origin')) - a request GET/POST value, kept when it is same-origin or starts with /
notes.sink: airflow/www/templates/airflow/trigger.html:66 onclick="location.href = '{{ origin }}'; return false" - the value sits in a JavaScript string inside an HTML attribute
notes.between: the trigger view passes origin into the template for every render; Django autoescaping turns ' into ', but the HTML parser decodes entities in the attribute before the JavaScript is parsed, so a quote in an allowed same-origin path closes the string and the rest of the value runs as script. The fix makes the cancel button a plain <a href="{{ origin }}">, where HTML escaping is the correct context. Second explanation: source.
notes.fix: replaces the onclick JavaScript with a plain anchor href on the cancel button

notes.between: Django autoescaping is on, but an unquoted attribute ends at the first space, so a parameter such as ?name=x%20onmouseover=alert(1) escapes the value and adds an attribute.
